attributes.body:
Often, the adverbial particle か is used in the middle of a sentence, in the same way that it is as a sentence ending particle. The main differences are as follows:

Adverbial Particle: 副助詞（ふくじょし） - Highlights uncertain things '不確（ふたし）かであること'. This is the same か as in どこか 'somewhere'.

Sentence Ending Particle: 終助詞（しゅうじょし） - Highlights doubts and questions '疑問（ぎもん）や質問（しつもん）'. This is a direct question.

In the case of the adverbial particle か and 'uncertain things', this will almost always be followed by a word that is seeking information about the uncertain thing.

As can be seen in these examples, sometimes the adverbial particle will appear by itself, and sometimes it will appear together with the sentence ending particle in the same sentence. However, due to the 'uncertainty' being displayed by the adverbial particle, the question marker at the end of the sentence is not required.

Caution

This か should not be preceded by だ (or です), this is why words like どこか and 誰（だれ）か are not どこだか and 誰（だれ）だか.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: Question Words in a Noun Clause

attributes.body: Both are embedded question forms. A question phrase plus か makes an indirect question, like 何時に来るか分からない ('I don't know what time they'll come'). かどうか focuses specifically on yes/no questions, like 来るかどうか分からない ('I don't know whether or not they'll come.').

The 誰か・どこか・誰も・どこも pattern combines question words like 誰 ('who') and どこ ('where') with particles to express ideas like 'someone' or 'somewhere.' These forms are also related to how the particle か is used with question phrases in embedded questions. For example, 誰が来るか分かりますか？ means 'Do you know who will come?'

first_relatable.slug: 誰か-どこか-誰も-どこも
first_relatable.title: 誰か・どこか・誰も・どこも
first_relatable.meaning: Someone, Somewhere, Not anyone, Not anywhere

attributes.body: Question-phrase + か embeds a question, e.g. 来るか分からない ('I don't know if they're coming.'). か〜ないかのうちに expresses something happening immediately at a moment of uncertainty, e.g. 来るか来ないかのうちに 'just as they arrived'.

second_relatable.title: か〜ないかのうちに
second_relatable.meaning: Right after, As soon as, Just when, Barely

attributes.body: Both uses of か are extensions of its basic function as a question particle. When following a Wh-question word (like who, what, where, why, how), it creates a phrase meaning 'some-(word)' (e.g., 誰か = 'someone,' どこか = 'somewhere,' いつか = 'sometime'). When following regular nouns, it means 'or' (e.g., 今日か明日休みます = 'I'll take off today or tomorrow').

The なにか・なにも pattern combines the question word なに with particles to express ideas like 'something' or 'nothing.' This structure is based on how the particle か is used with question words within a sentence. For example, 何が食べたいか分かりますか？ means 'Do you know what (they) want to eat?'

first_relatable.title: なにか・なにも
first_relatable.meaning: Something, Nothing, Anything, Not anything, Some kind of, Not any kind of
